name.en: Clone or unlicensed firm claiming to be licensed in Malta

how.en: Fake firms copy the name, address or website of a real MFSA-licensed company, or simply claim to be registered in Malta, to sell investments, crypto or other financial services. They may cold-call or message you, and some copy the MFSA’s own website. Money sent to them is very likely lost.

text.en: A firm contacts you or you find its website, and it says it is licensed in Malta.
It offers investment or crypto services with attractive returns.
It asks you to send money to open an account.

Dear client, we are an MFSA-regulated investment house based in Sliema. Our managed portfolios return 8–12% per quarter. To open your account, complete the attached form and transfer the minimum €1,000 deposit.

en: firm says it is licensed in Malta
company copying a real Maltese firm
A firm you can’t find on the MFSA register, or whose contact details differ from the register.
Unexpected calls or messages offering investment advice.
A website address that only looks like the real firm’s or the MFSA’s.
Check the firm on the MFSA Financial Services Register and contact it only through the details listed there.
If you are dealing with one, stop all payments and contact the MFSA and the Police.
